Try Grok 4.6 image & video understanding, it’s a major upgrade!

Grok 4.6 multimodal is a step change from Grok 4.5. It’s one of the under-discussed improvements, and I’ve been very impressed by it.

I’ve had my @Tesla for 9 days—and it’s already saved my life. Full Self-Driving with HW4 is mind-blowing.

My car drove me ~800 miles from Georgia to Texas without me touching the wheel or pedals, while avoiding multiple collisions.

I’ve never felt safer in a vehicle.

Here’s one example of a collision avoided, automatically captured on camera.

In this instance (though it doesn’t show my actual POV), sparks covered the windshield, lighting up the road like the Fourth of July and obstructing my view. Since I was in FSD, the car reacted immediately without overcorrecting like I likely would have, which could have led to a far worse outcome.

Everyone who’s ridden with me and experienced FSD for the first time is blown away and now looking into buying one—including my parents, who like me have never owned an EV.

There’s no telling how many lives this technology will save. This is hands-down the most incredible purchase I’ve ever made.

God bless @elonmusk & the Tesla team🫡

The OpenAI Foundation is launching AI for Civil Society and Philanthropy to help nonprofits, community organizations, and other trusted partners put advanced AI to work on urgent challenges, develop practical solutions and scale what works.

The first effort is a $100 million commitment with Common Health Coalition to launch Breakthroughs to Follow-through to help care teams use AI to reach more patients with proven treatments - starting with the goal of doubling hepatitis C cure rates in Alabama, Illinois, Louisiana, and Massachusetts. Breakthroughs to Follow-through will work to identify patients who have fallen out of care, synthesize records, track progress, and focus limited staff time where it can have the greatest impact.

The OpenAI Foundation wants to empower those who are closest to issues and to put AI to work where it can make a meaningful difference in people’s lives.

items.text:
The vast majority of people care about animal welfare, but factory farming continues growing. Will animals always suffer?

In a brilliant new piece @KojiFlynnDo & @MartinVGould argue there’s a Kuznets curve for animal welfare: we can turn things around. worksinprogress.co/issue/wil…

• Demand for meat rises with wealth – South Korea went from eating about 4kg of meat per person per year in the 1960s to 120kg now. But rich countries often plateau at around 150kg per person per year, and in some, it’s begun to decline.
• Factory farming follows wealth. More than 80 billion land animals are slaughtered every year, and including fish more than doubles that number.
• Animals are one of the clearest examples where welfare has gotten worse over the long term.

It doesn’t have to stay this way. Like the classic Kuznets curve, where industrialization once meant worsening pollution, rich countries have managed to turn things around, cleaning the air we breathe; we can do the same for animal welfare.

Some improvements to farm animal welfare would be very cheap: it costs just 1-2 cents extra per egg for hens to be cage-free, and now 45% of hens in the US, 62% in the EU and 82% in the UK are.

Alternative meats are currently more expensive, but cheaper methods might reduce their costs like previous technological cost curves have done.

But there are other reforms too: in-ovo sexing, for example, involves identifying the sex of chicks while still in the egg, could spare the billions of male chicks each year who are gassed or ground up on their first day of life.

I learnt a lot from this article and loved it. Let’s bend the curve! You can read it in full here: worksinprogress.co/issue/wil…
